svg.text: Simplified hypothalamic and brainstem circuit. Colour marks the source system; arrowheads mean excitation, flat bars mean inhibition.

g.text: melatonin feedback: dampens evening SCN alerting (MT1) and shifts clock phase (MT2)
melatonin timing: SCN → PVN → spinal cord → superior cervical ganglion → pineal
Circadian signals reach the switch mainly through the SCN → vSPZ → DMH relay rather than by direct SCN projections. In the active phase the DMH inhibits VLPO and excites orexin neurons.
REM is gated by a second flip-flop: REM-off cells (vlPAG/LPT, helped by LC, raphe and orexin) inhibit REM-on SLD neurons, which also drive atonia through the medulla.
Active phase = daytime in humans; the DMH wiring was mapped mainly in nocturnal rodents, so its timing in people is inferred.
Melatonin signals darkness, not sleep (it rises in the active phase of nocturnal species); in humans it favours sleep indirectly, via the SCN and cooling.
Abbreviations: SCN suprachiasmatic nucleus; vSPZ ventral subparaventricular zone; DMH dorsomedial hypothalamus; PVN paraventricular nucleus; VLPO/MnPO ventrolateral/median preoptic nucleus;
LC locus coeruleus; TMN tuberomammillary nucleus; VTA ventral tegmental area; BF basal forebrain; PPT/LDT pedunculopontine/laterodorsal tegmental nuclei; SLD sublaterodorsal nucleus;
vlPAG ventrolateral periaqueductal grey; LPT lateral pontine tegmentum; ipRGC intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cell; TRH thyrotropin-releasing hormone.
Sources: Saper et al. 2005 (Nature) and 2010 (Neuron); Chou et al. 2003 (J Neurosci); Lu et al. 2006 (Nature); Yamanaka et al. 2003 (Neuron).
